The work zone will be located between Sawyer Road and Dawn Drive, just east of Highway 87, as contractor C.W. Roberts Contracting installs a new turn lane for a subdivision development project. item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County motorists should expect intermittent lane closures on Nichols Lake Road beginning tomorrow, starting Thursday, November 12. The work zone will be located between Sawyer Road and Dawn Drive, just east of Highway 87, as contractor C.W. Roberts Contracting installs a new turn lane for a subdivision development project.

County officials say flaggers will be positioned at each end of the work area to direct traffic and improve safety. Drivers passing through should exercise caution and be prepared for possible delays during construction hours.

According to Santa Rosa County, the project is slated to wrap up by December 18, weather permitting. For a detailed map of the affected area, Santa Rosa County has posted resources on its website.

item.content:encoded:
Two local artists are launching Recreation Art Supply, a pop-up shop designed to make creative materials more accessible and affordable for Pensacola's art community. Reema Eqab and Raylene Solis are centralizing used art supplies to lower the cost barrier for aspiring and established creatives who might otherwise struggle to afford traditional retail prices.

The concept addresses a real gap in the local market — quality art materials can be expensive, and the pop-up model allows the pair to test the idea while building community support. By focusing on used and repurposed supplies, Recreation Art Supply also promotes sustainability while serving artists across skill levels.

The shop reflects growing interest in Pensacola's creative economy and grassroots entrepreneurship. For anyone in the area looking for affordable art supplies or wanting to support local artists, the pop-up offers both practical access and a chance to connect with the creative community.

item.content:encoded:
The Pensacola Opera is reviving its Brown Bag Opera program, offering locals a chance to enjoy arias and theater selections during their lunch break, according to a news release reported by WKRG News 5.

The series brings live opera performance to a casual, accessible format — attendees can bring their own lunch and enjoy professional opera in an informal setting. The next Brown Bag Opera performance is scheduled for Tuesday, November 18.

The return of the program marks another offering from the Pensacola Opera's community engagement lineup, giving music and theater enthusiasts an opportunity to experience live performance without the formality of a full evening at the opera house.

item.content:encoded:

item.content:encoded:
A historic structure with deep roots in Baldwin County has found a new home. The Montrose Hermit Hut, a significant piece of local heritage, was transported through Fairhope this week to the Flying Creek Nature Preserve, where it will be preserved for future generations.

The move represents a collaborative effort to protect the hut's legacy and ensure the structure remains accessible to the public. Flying Creek Nature Preserve officials say the relocation will allow the hut to be properly maintained and integrated into the preserve's educational and historical offerings.

While Fairhope is just across the state line in Alabama, the story reflects the interconnected nature of Gulf Coast communities and their shared commitment to preserving regional history.

item.content:encoded:
VetCV held a grand opening Wednesday for its newest Mission Next Center at Pensacola State College's Warrington campus, marking the organization's expansion of veteran support services in the region.

The new center is VetCV's second Mission Next location. The first opened in Milton about a year ago and has already served nearly 400 veterans and their families, according to WKRG News 5.

The Mission Next Centers provide support and resources for veterans transitioning to civilian life. With the Pensacola State location now operational, VetCV aims to reach more veterans across Escambia and Santa Rosa counties.

item.content:encoded: The University of Texas women's soccer team pulled off a major postseason upset Wednesday, defeating previously-unbeaten Vanderbilt in a tournament game played in Pensacola. The victory marked the first time Texas has defeated a No. 1-ranked team, according to NCAA soccer analyst Jon Rothstein. Margueritte Bates led the Longhorns' effort in what Rothstein described as "maybe the upset of the postseason." The win sets up a potentially formidable Texas squad as the tournament continues, with Rothstein suggesting few teams will want to face the Longhorns moving forward.

item.title: Baptist Heart & Vascular hits 1,000 TAVR procedures since 2014
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Baptist Heart & Vascular Institute announced Tuesday that it has completed its 1,000th Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) procedure, marking more than a decade of providing minimally invasive heart valve treatment to patients in Northwest Florida. TAVR is used to treat severe aortic stenosis, a serious heart valve condition that causes…
item.content:encoded:
Baptist Heart & Vascular Institute announced Tuesday that it has completed its 1,000th Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement (TAVR) procedure, marking more than a decade of providing minimally invasive heart valve treatment to patients in Northwest Florida.

TAVR is used to treat severe aortic stenosis, a serious heart valve condition that causes shortness of breath, fatigue, and limits physical activity. Before the procedure became available, open-heart surgery was the standard treatment option. The catheter-based approach allows physicians to replace a diseased valve without major surgery, leading to faster recovery and improved quality of life for patients.

Baptist became the first facility in Florida's Panhandle to offer TAVR when it launched the program in 2014. The 1,000th patient, John Luetkemeyer, reported significant improvement after the procedure. "I have less shortness of breath, and I am able to walk greater distances," Luetkemeyer said in a statement. The procedure is performed by a team of interventional cardiologists, cardiovascular surgeons, nurses, and support staff.

Interventional Cardiologist Luther Carter, M.D., noted that the vast majority of aortic valve patients now receive treatment without open-heart surgery. "I've been hearing it for more than 12 years, and it's pretty amazing that it's the same story over and over again about patient's improved quality of life," Carter said.

item.title: Escambia County Warns of Scams Targeting Amendment 3 Homestead Exemption
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County officials are alerting residents to fraudulent schemes preying on property owners who may be eligible for homestead exemption benefits under Florida's newly approved Amendment 3. Scammers are impersonating staff from Property Appraiser's Offices and attempting to harvest Social Security numbers and other personal information…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County officials are alerting residents to fraudulent schemes preying on property owners who may be eligible for homestead exemption benefits under Florida's newly approved Amendment 3. Scammers are impersonating staff from Property Appraiser's Offices and attempting to harvest Social Security numbers and other personal information through unsolicited calls, texts, and messages.

The county emphasizes that legitimate Property Appraiser offices will never contact property owners by phone to request personal information. Residents who qualify for the exemption changes under Amendment 3 will have their eligibility processed automatically—no action or response is needed on their part.

Anyone who receives a suspicious call, text, or email claiming to represent the Property Appraiser's Office should not click any links or provide personal data. Residents with questions about legitimate exemptions can contact the Escambia County Property Appraiser's Office directly at 850-434-2735.

If you've already been contacted by scammers, report the incident to the Federal Trade Commission at reportfraud.ftc.gov.

item.title: American Airlines braces for record Thanksgiving travel, 8M passengers expected
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: American Airlines is preparing for one of its busiest travel periods in years, expecting to carry more than 8 million customers across nearly 85,000 flights between November 19 and December 1, according to a company press release issued Monday. The carrier's largest single operating day since the pandemic will be Sunday, November 29, when American…
item.content:encoded:
American Airlines is preparing for one of its busiest travel periods in years, expecting to carry more than 8 million customers across nearly 85,000 flights between November 19 and December 1, according to a company press release issued Monday.

The carrier's largest single operating day since the pandemic will be Sunday, November 29, when American plans to fly 7,021 flights. The Thanksgiving travel season traditionally represents a major revenue and operational challenge for airlines, with tight scheduling and weather volatility adding complexity to an already demanding period.

For Pensacola-area travelers, the forecast suggests full flights and potential delays during peak travel windows around the Thanksgiving holiday and immediately after. Passengers planning to fly during this window should expect congestion at Pensacola International Airport and may want to book flights outside the heaviest travel days—typically the day before Thanksgiving and the Sunday after.

item.content:encoded:
A new urgent care clinic is set to open its doors in Pensacola this week, according to the City of Pensacola. Patients First urgent care will begin operations Wednesday, Nov. 11, adding another healthcare option for residents and visitors needing non-emergency medical services in the Gulf Coast area.

The facility's opening comes as the Pensacola area continues to see growth in healthcare infrastructure. While details about the clinic's specific location and services remain limited, urgent care facilities typically handle injuries, minor illnesses, and other conditions that don't require a full emergency room visit, often with shorter wait times and lower costs than traditional hospital ERs.

More information about Patients First urgent care's hours, services, and insurance acceptance should be available as the clinic opens this week.
